sources.title: Somalia Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), Somalia Humanitarian Country Team, and Somali Disaster Management Agency
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 shock and displacement observations; 2026 humanitarian needs, response planning and access conditions.
sources.methodology: Multi-agency plan synthesizes assessments, displacement tracking and access mapping.
sources.limitations: Operational snapshot; estimates are not climate attribution or independent causal evaluation.

sources.title: Endline Evaluation Report: Building Resilient Communities in Somalia (BRCiS) III
sources.organization: Causal Design, prepared for the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
sources.temporal_coverage: BRCiS III baseline 2024 and endline 2026; programme closed on 31 March 2026.
sources.methodology: Panel survey, focus groups and contribution analysis: 3,889 households across 21 districts.
sources.limitations: Non-counterfactual, self-reported programme results; early closure limits attribution and follow-up.

sources.title: Burning Ground: Tackling Climate Change and Conflict in South-central Somalia
sources.temporal_coverage: Deegan Bile project period and drought context 2021-2024; SIPRI surveys and focus groups in January 2024.
sources.methodology: Literature review, IOM partnership, over 700 survey respondents and six focus groups.
sources.limitations: Close partnership may affect objectivity; 18-month projects; Hirshabelle evaluation was pending.

claims.paraphrase: The HNRP reports a fourth failed northern rainy season in 2025, rainfall 60% below average, 80% of Puntland berkads dry and 50 Hirshabelle boreholes needing repair.
claims.limitations: Operational figures do not establish climate attribution or uniform state conditions.

claims.paraphrase: Climate- and conflict-linked shocks displaced 680,000 people in 2025; DTM projected over 200,000 more by year-end, 52% drought-linked and 44% conflict-linked. Nearly 200,000 IDPs faced high eviction risk from land disputes and weak tenure.
claims.scenario: DTM forecast to year-end 2026; no projection scenario specified.
affected_groups: households exposed to drought and conflict
claims.limitations: Dated operational estimate, not independent causal attribution.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: OCHA attributes displacement to both drought and conflict.

claims.paraphrase: In 2025, checkpoints, ambushes, IEDs, hostilities and road decay constrained humanitarian routes in the Shabelle corridor, Hiraan, Bay, Bakool and Lower Juba.
claims.limitations: Humanitarian access only, not adaptation coverage.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: OCHA says conflict and climate shocks restrict aid presence and mobility.

claims.locator: PDF p. 7, executive summary, context and shocks.
claims.paraphrase: BRCiS panel households reporting drought rose from 15% in 2024 to 67% in 2026 as the main shock shifted from El Niño floods to prolonged drought.

claims.locator: PDF p. 82, section 3.6, conflict's toll on markets and wellbeing.
claims.paraphrase: In Afgoye's Jambaluul and Buula Madino, conflict kept residents from farms and markets, compounding drought losses; 30% said conflict blocked market travel.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Conflict constrained farm and market access during drought.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: PDF p. 82, section 3.6, conflict's toll on markets and wellbeing.

claims.paraphrase: Conflict or insecurity stopped meeting attendance for 52.1% of surveyed BRCiS cooperative members (n=526).

claims.locator: PDF p. 79, section 3.7.3, agroecological training and water access.
claims.paraphrase: El Barde Town and Emilow gardens flourished with borehole/drip water; water-scarce Higlowayn, Lawareeg and Ayeeyo reported little uptake.
BRCiS panel resilience index rose from 3.24 to 3.71; market and ecosystem scores improved more than leadership.

claims.locator: PDF p. 22, section 4, locally legitimate natural resource management.
claims.paraphrase: SIPRI says IOM's Galmudug evaluation found fewer target-area conflicts after resource committees formed, citing faster dispute response than formal authorities; it also reports broader women/youth participation in resource decisions.
affected_groups: women and youth participating in resource decisions
claims.limitations: Unpublished IOM partner evaluation, not independent causal evidence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: IOM linked reduced conflict to faster committee response.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: PDF p. 22, section 4, locally legitimate natural resource management.

claims.locator: PDF p. 23, section 4, cross-clan collaboration and women's participation.
claims.paraphrase: In Duqaqo, women trained in environmental peacebuilding proposed a drip-irrigated communal farm; after leaders resisted, a peaceful demonstration led to land being designated.
claims.limitations: Single qualitative case; long-term effects unmeasured.

claims.paraphrase: SIPRI warns that water projects could overuse groundwater or trigger competition over borehole and reservoir control, especially during drought or dry seasons.
claims.scenario: Conditional drought/dry-season risk; no formal scenario or probability stated.
claims.limitations: Conditional risk warning, not observed conflict incidence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: SIPRI links new water sources to control competition in drought seasons.

search_audit.outcome: Found route-specific humanitarian access constraints in the HNRP and BRCiS survey evidence that conflict/insecurity limited market, farm and cooperative participation. These findings concern humanitarian access and programme participation, not proof that adaptation was stopped nationally.

search_audit.outcome: Found a full independent endline evaluation measuring resilience shifts and documenting water-conditioned garden uptake, resource constraints and conflict-related limits on producer-cooperative attendance.

gaps: The Somalia HNRP is a dated operational snapshot; access, displacement, needs and conflict conditions may change quickly, and some inaccessible areas are likely under-observed.
The BRCiS III baseline PDF was too large for the available reader; claims use the accessible endline evaluation and its stated baseline comparisons, not the unavailable baseline text.
The BRCiS results cover 21 programme districts, not all Somalia; the endline is non-counterfactual and includes self-reported outcomes.
SIPRI's local conflict-reduction claim relies on an unpublished IOM Galmudug final report; the Hirshabelle evaluation was pending when SIPRI wrote, and project duration was only 18 months.

No evidence in these new sources estimates nationally the amount of climate adaptation or resilience programming prevented by insecurity; the HNRP documents humanitarian access restrictions and BRCiS documents specific activity/market participation barriers.

Subnational evidence is concentrated in south-central programme areas and 2025 drought-affected regions; current climate-security outcomes for coastal communities, fisheries, minority groups and people in inaccessible territories remain thin.
